messages:
maria: Heads-up — noticed steady memory growth on prod-rt-2 over the last 12h. KV resident pages for tenant:t42 keep climbing even though eviction rates are high. attaching quick pprof snippet below.

ashwin: Can you paste the pprof top? curious if it's live objects or leaked pinned pages.

maria: quick dump: `pprof --alloc_space profile.pb.gz` top:
```
flat  flat%   sum%        cum   cum%
120MB  24.0% 24.0%   120MB 24.0%  kv::Page::allocate
80MB   16.0% 40.0%   200MB 40.0%  slab::Fragment::retain
40MB    8.0% 48.0%   240MB 48.0%  kv::Page::pin
```

jamie: That looks like fragmentation: a lot of small fragments kept pinned. Are we seeing a high churn in large-context requests that pin pages for longctx?

maria: yes — correlated with requests that have seq_len > 10k tokens (mostly long-recall jobs). Those tenants have spikey access patterns causing cold pages to be repeatedly re-pinned, preventing reuse.

leo: Two actionable items IMHO: 1) add a background compaction job that tries to coalesce small free fragments into larger contiguous runs; 2) implement a lease timeout for pinned pages so longctx can't hold forever.

ashwin: For (2) want to be careful — timeouts can break correctness for some customers relying on KV residency semantics. Maybe make it a per-tenant soft quota with a grace period + warning, not a hard evict.

maria: agreed. propose algorithm: eviction_score = age_ms * (1 + frag_penalty) / (1 + reuse_count) - lease_boost
Frag penalty computed from small-slab ratio. If eviction_score > threshold && tenant_used_pct > quota -> mark for compaction/evict. Pseudo: 
```
score = age_ms * (1 + frag_ratio*2) / max(1, reuse_count)
if tenant_pct > soft_quota and score > Q: preemptively throttle tenant
```

jamie: Also saw a perf regression last week after the kernel-selection change that switched to 4KiB->16KiB page grouping in some configs. That increased external fragmentation for multi-tenant workloads. Could be related. commit: `a1b2c3f`

leo: Good catch. If kernel selection aligns pages differently, compaction becomes more expensive. We should revert or add an isolation bypass: for multi-tenant noisy cases, prefer smaller page-granularity kernels.

maria: short-term ops plan:
- enable tenant soft-quota alert for >70% residency for 15m
- run nightly `kv-evict-sim` with current access traces to estimate compaction benefit
- prototype lease-timeout config behind feature flag for a few noisy tenants

infra-bot: rollout-checklist created: https://redwood.internal/tasks/EVCT-783 (assigned to @maria) :white_check_mark:

ashwin: +1 on simulated run. can we also add a metric for fragment-size-histogram per-tenant? that'll help decide compaction thresholds.

maria: will add histograms and wire a dashboard. If the sim shows >15% reclaimable space on noisy tenants, we'll enable compaction job w/ staged canary.

jamie: also raising a short-term mitigation: add API-level backpressure — token-bucket per-tenant for longctx requests. That buys time for compaction and avoids cascade.

leo: note for design doc: include interactions with Dedicated pools — dedicated GPU/pool tenants should opt-out of soft quotas and compaction by default. Need wording for customer config.

maria: thanks all. I'll push a small PR with the alert + sim job config, and post results tomorrow.

infra-bot: PR created: https://redwood.internal/pulls/4521 (maria) — CI queued.

maria: (follow-up) if anyone has longctx traces for tenant:t42 please DM me, trying to reproduce pinned-page pattern locally. :mag:
